subject: SLO alignment & maintenance handoff — OptiFin MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Evan Price <evan.price@optifin.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@optifin.com>, OptiFin Legal <legal@optifin.com>
Date: 2027-08-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: OptiFin MSA redlines — uptime & maintenance

Michael — attaching our redlines for the MSA and order form. High level asks:
- Uptime: we need a 99.99% SLA for the endpoints used in production (latency-sensitive routing).
- Service credits: straight percentage credits with no unilateral cap; prefer cumulative credits up to 100% for sustained outages.
- Response windows: Sev1 acknowledged within 30 minutes, remediation ETA within 4 hours.
- Planned maintenance: max 4 hours per month during business hours only (we're in finance and need minimal nightly work). 7-day notice for planned maintenance.
- Emergency maintenance: allowed only with 4 hours notice and detailed postmortem within 48 hours.

Please review and confirm which items Redwood can accept vs. request modifications. We attached a redline PDF and an uptime sample metric set for reference.

Attachments: OptiFin_MSA_redlines_20270813.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Evan Price
Head of IT Operations | OptiFin
ev an.price@optifin.com
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-13T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: FW: OptiFin MSA redlines — need counteroffer

FW: Evan's redlines (see attached). Quick ask: legal/ops — can we carve a pragmatic counter that preserves our ability to operate, gives Ops assurances, and keeps price predictability?

Proposed Redwood counter (first pass):
- Monthly uptime (rolling 30d): 99.95% for core generation endpoints; 99.90% for embeddings.
- Service credits (monthly): 5% for 99.0–99.95, 15% for 98.0–99.0, 30% for <98.0; cumulative cap 30% of monthly fees.
- Severity response SLAs: Sev1 (system down/high impact) — acknowledgement within 1 hour, mitigation ETA within 4 hours; Sev2 — ack within 4 hours, mitigation ETA 24 hours; Sev3 — ack within 24 hours.
- Planned maintenance: standard window Sun 02:00–06:00 PT, 48-hour notice for routine maintenance.
- Emergency maintenance: permitted to protect customer data/avoid broader outages; we will give as much notice as possible and provide postmortem within 72 hours. Emergency maintenance does not trigger credits except in demonstrable data loss cases.

Attached: uptime-matrix-v2.xlsx (shows measurement method).

Can you each call out hard blockers and suggested language edits? If we can agree internally by EOD tomorrow, I'll send a summarized counter to Evan.

Thanks — Michael
Michael Grant
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: OptiFin MSA redlines — need counteroffer

Michael / team — reviewed Evan's PDF and your draft. Legal POV and a few suggested compromises below:

1) Uptime buckets:
   - Accept 99.95% for core endpoints; accept 99.90% for embeddings as you proposed. Call out exact metric: availability measured as successful 2xx responses over total requests, excluding scheduled maintenance windows and excluded events.

2) Credits & cap:
   - Propose a two-tier credits approach with a reasonable cap to avoid open-ended exposure: 7% monthly fee for 99.0–99.95; 20% monthly fee for <99.0; cap credits at 40% per 12-month period (not per month). This addresses their ask for cumulative but limits company risk.

3) Response & remediation:
   - Push back slightly on 30-minute Sev1 ack. We can offer 1 hour ack and active mitigation within 4 hours as standard. Include escalation matrix with names/roles and SLA-driven routing to dedicated on-call for Dedicated customers; for Hosted customers specify remote-runbook-driven response.

4) Maintenance windows:
   - Counter: Planned maintenance limited to 6 hours per month; preferred maintenance window Sun 02:00–06:00 PT (same as draft) with 72 hours notice for non-critical updates.
   - Emergency maintenance: allow with as much notice as possible; require postmortem within 48 hours. State that emergency maintenance is excluded from credits unless caused by Redwood negligence.

5) Measurement & dispute:
   - Add clause: customers may request contestation of uptime calculations; disputes handled via mutual good faith review; final measurement uses our telemetry with exported dashboards (link in order form).

Next steps: I'll draft contract language for Section 3 (SLA) and Section 7 (service credits & measurement). Ben — can you confirm whether a 48h postmortem is operationally realistic? If yes, we'll include.

Marissa
Director, Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: OptiFin MSA redlines — need counteroffer

Agree with Marissa. Operational notes:
- 48h postmortem is OK for most incidents; for full root cause analysis we may take longer, but a preliminary postmortem within 48h is realistic.
- We'll add a mitigation/backup commitment in the order form: if core endpoints degrade we will route traffic to quantized fallback model for up to 2 hours to preserve availability (this is a best-effort, not a separate SLA).
- I'll update the order form SLO table and include a short appendix describing measurement method + sample metric queries.

Ben
Head of Support Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Price <evan.price@optifin.com>
Cc: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@optifin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: OptiFin MSA redlines — uptime & maintenance

Evan — thanks for the redlines and patience while we reviewed. Below is a concise summary of the counter we can agree to and the next steps. Please review and confirm whether OptiFin can accept this as the SLO addendum to the order form:

Redwood proposed SLO summary (counter):
- Availability (rolling 30d): Core generation endpoints — 99.95%; Embeddings — 99.90%. Measurement: 2xx success rate measured by Redwood telemetry, excluding scheduled maintenance and force majeure.
- Credits: 7% monthly fee if availability falls between 99.0–99.95; 20% monthly fee if <99.0. Credits capped at 40% over any 12-month period.
- Response SLAs: Sev1 — acknowledgement within 1 hour, mitigation ETA within 4 hours; Sev2 — ack 4 hours, mitigation 24 hours; Sev3 — ack 24 hours.
- Planned maintenance: 6 hours/month standard window Sun 02:00–06:00 PT; 72-hour notice required for routine maintenance.
- Emergency maintenance: permitted to protect integrity/avoid wider outages; Redwood will provide postmortem within 48 hours. Emergency maintenance excluded from credits except in cases of Redwood negligence.
- Operational mitigations: during partial degradations Redwood will attempt routing to fallback model variants where feasible (best-effort).

Attachments: orderform-slo-summary-20270815.pdf (pdf) — includes redline snippets and SLO table for insertion into the order form. Also attached our uptime matrix that defines calculation windows.

If this is acceptable, please confirm and we'll generate an Order Form that incorporates the SLO addendum and send a DocuSign packet. If OptiFin still needs a higher uptime (99.99) we can discuss a dedicated reserved-capacity offering and an adjusted pricing attachment.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: orderform-slo-summary-20270815.pdf, uptime-matrix-v2.xlsx
